answers.question: Q1
answers.correction: The count holds: four of the nine state the identification and five do not. Three wordings are stronger than the papers. (a) 'always credited to Minic 2020 and Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2021': only the Snowmass paper cites both ([29, 30]). 2202.06890 ([11]) and Addazi et al. ([408]) cite Minic 2020 alone. 2011.08852's sentence cites the modified-dark-matter papers [55] and [26–30], of which [29] includes Minic 2020; BHM 2021 is its [46], cited elsewhere in the paper. (b) 'always as a proposal': Addazi §2.3.4 lists the duals 'associated with dark matter degrees of freedom' among 'observable hallmarks', and the Snowmass paper states 'dark matter should be viewed as a dual SM' as the group's approach. The reader's own details (1) and (3) say this; its summary sentence does not. (c) 'each describes it as the dual spacetime' holds for the four that state the identification only: 2212.00901 and 2303.17495 use x̃ for the momentum coordinate of a modular cell, 2202.05266 has no dual, and 2312.00409 does not describe one.

answers.question: Q4
answers.correction: Accurate for the nine. The full text of the modified-dark-matter review supports the reading of 'correlated': its §2 ties the dark-matter mass profile to the baryonic one through a₀. Two qualifications. (1) One of 2202.06890's two sources does speculate on couplings beyond gravity: Ho, Minic and Ng 2010 (its [45]) say couplings of MONDian dark matter to Standard Model particles 'could be nonstandard'. (2) The question the reader left to Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2021 is answered in that paper (arXiv:2010.15610). A coupling (λ⁸/L¹⁰)[φ, φ̃] 'as predicted by the doubled/non-commutative set-up' gives 'an explicit correlation between the dark matter sector and a visible sector' (§5). The correlation 'becomes invisible in effective field theory, and it vanishes as either λ→0 or L→∞' (§4). So within the school, 'correlated' covers both the observed scaling and a non-gravitational coupling term suppressed by λ⁸/L¹⁰.
counter_evidence: 1709.04388 §2: 'dark matter exists in our scheme, but its mass profile is tied to the baryonic mass profile (at least on galactic scales) via the observed acceleration and the fundamental acceleration parameter, set by the cosmological constant.' (FOUND)

answers.question: Q10
answers.correction: Every number reproduces in independent code. Four corrections. (1) The opening 'In all of these papers dark energy is the geometry or curvature of the dual spacetime' is too broad. 2202.05266 has no dual spacetime, and 2212.00901 and 2303.17495 bound the vacuum energy by counting modular cells. (2) In the w ≥ −1 model the future meeting of the cutoffs is imposed by the authors ('We want … to meet at a>1'). My computation: eq. (21) read past the meeting gives a negative dark-energy density, ρ_Λ(1.2 a_meet) = −0.22 to −0.28 ρ* at the seven listed points. The paper does not discuss a > a_meet, so whether the model has negative or zero dark energy there is open; this bears on #11 §10's turnaround. (3) The paper states which cutoff motion gives which sign. Under relation (16), constant G_N gives w < −1; w > −1 needs Ẽ_UV falling and Ẽ_IR rising, which non-commutative RG flows 'in principle allow'. Its eq. (46) also takes our own UV cutoff to grow, E_UV = E_Planck·a. My computation (de_check_fixedUV.py) shows the sign comes from the IR relation alone: with E_UV fixed, w(1) = −0.818, −0.923, −0.899 at three listed points. record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3 'What differs': 'Their dual sector is correlated with ours by construction', supported by BHM 2023 (Symmetry) and by 2202.06890's 'Dark matter, dark energy and visible matter are naturally correlated in this description'; 'All three judges for C1 read this as predicting couplings between dark and visible matter beyond gravity'. record_contradictions.note: Right for 2202.06890's sentence. Its sources [45, 46] are modified-dark-matter papers, and [46]'s full text (1709.04388 §2) defines the correlation as the dark-matter mass profile 'tied to the baryonic mass profile' through a₀ (FOUND); the paper writes no coupling term. Two qualifications. (i) [45] itself speculates beyond gravity: '(2) The couplings of MONDian dark matter to the Standard Model particles could be nonstandard, and perhaps even of a spin-orbit type' (1005.3537, FOUND). So the reader's 'For these two sources, … couplings beyond gravity are the record's and the judges' readings, not the papers' words' is true of 2202.06890's text but not of its source. (ii) The record's 'by construction' has a direct source in the school, outside the reader's set. Berglund, Hübsch and Minic 2021 (arXiv:2010.15610) write 'the known Standard Model fields and their dark matter duals are dynamically correlated' (abstract). Their coupling (λ⁸/L¹⁰)[φ, φ̃] is 'as predicted by the doubled/non-commutative set-up, and provides an explicit correlation between the dark matter sector and a visible sector' (§5), and 'This correlation becomes invisible in effective field theory, and it vanishes as either λ→0 or L→∞' (§4; all FOUND). The record already cites BHM 2021 for the limit. It should rest 'by construction' on BHM 2021's coupling term, not on 2202.06890's parenthesis, and should say the term is suppressed by λ⁸/L¹⁰ and invisible in effective field theory.

overall: The reader's output is reliable on its sources. All 115 quotations are verbatim, the citations, reference numbers and arXiv dates check out, and every number it computed reproduces in independent code (w values, μ, the DESI mapping, the meeting scale). The corrections are of degree, not direction. One reading is wrong: the λ → 0 limit in 2011.08852, where the dual geometry still sets G_N and Λ. Several answers are stated more uniformly than the papers: who is credited, 'always a proposal', infinite statistics only for dark energy, and nothing selecting the modular cell's shape. The cited modified-dark-matter review, read only in abstract, expects future direct-detection and collider tests, and the Snowmass paper has 8 pages, not two. Of the three record items, the correlation item holds for 2202.06890, but the record's 'by construction' is supported by Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2021's explicit coupling term. The Hur et al. item holds for the literature-check note, but the record already states that paper's w > −1 model elsewhere, in a form that omits its phantom first model.
